### cavity2dSolver {#sec-example-laminar-cavity2dSolver}

This example solves the same lid-driven cavity as [[`laminar/cavity2d`](/examples/laminar/cavity2d/cavity2d.qmd)]{.content-visible when-format="html"}[`laminar/cavity2d` (@sec-example-laminar-cavity2d)]{.content-visible when-format="pdf"}: the governing equations, the boundary conditions, the domain, the discretization and the comparison with @GHIA1982387 are described there.
This page only describes how `cavity2dSolver` differs from it: the simulation is implemented with the solver class concept, a class derived from `LbSolver`, together with the XML parameter interface.

#### Solver class

In `cavity2d`, `main()` calls free functions for every step of the simulation and runs the time loop itself.
Here, `main()` only reads the XML file, creates the solver and starts it:

```{.cpp}
XMLreader config( "cavity2d.xml" );
auto cavity2d = createLbSolver<Cavity2dSolver<T>> (config);
cavity2d->solve();
```

#### Files

```
cavity2dSolver/
├── cavity2d.cpp               Cavity2dSolver class and main(): reads cavity2d.xml, creates and runs the solver
├── cavity2d.xml               parameters of the simulation and of the output
├── description_cavity2d.xml   description of the parameters for OpenGPI
└── Makefile
```

The results are written to `tmp/` in the directory the example is run from: `vtkData/cavity2d.pvd` opens all time steps in ParaView, `imageData/` holds the velocity heat maps and `gnuplotData/` the comparisons with Ghia et al. The heat maps and plots are drawn with gnuplot; without it, only the data in `gnuplotData/data/` is written.
